controls.historical_region: Calais, Guînes, Hames and English Pale of Calais
controls.effective_authority: Governor of Calais and English officers/garrisons
documented_control_fact: English garrison/royal treasury/staple and marcher settlements continued with local courts and border-defense structures; frontier edges changed by royal works and war.
Original town/castle and selected surrounding strongpoints are stronger proofs than a fully outlined March polygon.

spatial.historical_area_basis: Use c1500 prior research hypothesis as starting point, but the later 1525 commission shows frontier contest; do not mechanically retain a 10-year fixed polygon

controls.historical_region: English Pale around Dublin and certain legal/government boroughs
controls.legal_claimant: Henry VIII as Lord of Ireland
controls.effective_authority: Gerald FitzGerald VIII Earl Kildare (to 1513), Gerald IX Earl (1513–19), then Lord Surrey appointed 1519
documented_control_fact: Kildare VIII deputy reappointed 1510-11-08; successor IX earl Lord Deputy from late 1513 until dismissal in 1519.
Local Gaelic lords and rival urban/pale factions held powers beyond shifting effective Pale boundary; four shire limits are not 1510 actual maps.

spatial.historical_area_basis: Inherited 1488 legal defensive line should be dashed historical proxy, not continuous decade-long actual tax district

controls.historical_region: Tournai city (today Belgium), English king's French dominion
controls.legal_claimant: Henry VIII as claimant King of France (title used for occupation); France contested
controls.effective_authority: Crown-appointed English garrison/governor and locally retained municipal institutions

unknown_transition_days: If 1519 shows as snapshot post-February, former English occupation layer must disappear.

documented_control_fact: 23 Sep 1513 city capitulation to Henry VIII forces; Tudor government and local municipality functioned under English royal authority.
Treaty for cession dated 4 October 1518; actual physical return Feb 1519 in Neil Murphy's scholarly reconstruction.
Henry VIII ruled Tournai separately from England, in his claimed capacity as king of France; not incorporated into English parliamentary constituencies.

spatial.historical_area_basis: Use approximate historic city/tower point or small urban visual envelope with dashed outline; do not fill today's Tournai commune or bishopric

controls.effective_authority: English/Habsburg allied occupying forces during siege and aftermath; French after return
documented_control_fact: City capitulated around 23 Aug 1513 to Henry VIII and Maximilian forces; sections razed.
Local municipality states French King Francis I oversaw rebuilding walls by 1518: cannot claim long-lasting Tudor colonial civil administration during 1514–19.

spatial.historical_area_basis: Single temporary military event point with aftermath; no 1513–1519 persistent English area

controls.legal_claimant: English Crown; disputed in active war
controls.effective_authority: briefly forces of James IV of Scotland then English controlled again
documented_control_fact: Historic England scheduled monument record directly records Scots took Wark Castle before Flodden in 1513 and English king directed strengthening after campaign.
A captured fortress does not imply Northumberland county became Scottish Crown territory.

spatial.historical_area_basis: Point marker for short 1513 capture; after 1513 controlled by English Crown again and restoration surveyed 1517

controls.historical_region: Kingdom of Scotland under James IV, then minor James V
controls.effective_authority: Scottish Council, Margaret Tudor regency and John Duke of Albany (from 1515), with noble faction competition
documented_control_fact: Flodden English victory Sep 9 1513 killed James IV; James V became Scottish king and Scotland's own Crown, councils, treasury and laws continued.
1515 Albany regency and noble faction politics did not convert Scottish kingdom into an English territory.

spatial.historical_area_basis: Historical Scottish kingdom boundary based on sourced early modern maps, regional contest marked dashed; no new English orange fill

controls.historical_region: Orkney and Shetland and Scotland western Isles
controls.effective_authority: Scottish royal representatives in northern isles; Western Isles varied lordship/clans
documented_control_fact: Northern isles under Scottish Crown since 1472; Western Isles after 1493 forfeiture included substantial local power.
1513 Flodden did not transfer them to English sovereignty.

spatial.historical_area_basis: No assumption homogeneous continuous direct royal rule of all western isles; existing 1500s source package carries early island-specific records

controls.historical_region: Channel Islands and Isle of Man
controls.legal_claimant: English monarch as Crown lord of Channel Islands; Stanley lordship in Isle of Man
controls.effective_authority: Jersey/Guernsey bailiwicks; Isle of Man's local lord and Tynwald
documented_control_fact: Separate local laws and relationships with English Parliament, actual local government.
Imperial category should distinguish Crown dependencies from colonial conquest and ordinary English counties.

spatial.historical_area_basis: Use island locations with distinct pattern rather than England-region fill

controls.legal_claimant: O'Donnell family and competing Gaelic dynasties
controls.effective_authority: O'Donnell garrison left at Omagh in 1512 according to Irish annals
documented_control_fact: Annals of the Four Masters M1512.8 records O'Donnell rebuilt castle torn down earlier by Earl Kildare and left his own warders.
Gaelic control is active local political governance; English Crown cannot be portrayed as uniformly governing all Ulster.

spatial.historical_area_basis: Only site-level point once accurately geolocated, no whole Tyrone polygon

controls.legal_claimant: multiple Irish polities with an English royal deputy expedition
controls.effective_authority: Kildare deputy temporarily garrisoned Roscommon in 1512 according to Gaelic annal
documented_control_fact: M1512.9 records the royal deputy Kildare raided, took Roscommon, and left warders.
This is some evidence for a limited new local military foothold; end of garrison and extent of jurisdiction not confirmed.

spatial.historical_area_basis: Point or fortified urban site only, not County Roscommon orange

controls.historical_region: Sligo and adjacent castles, western Ireland
controls.legal_claimant: O'Donnell Gaelic political power versus rival Gaelic dynasties
controls.effective_authority: O'Donnell forces took Sligo and some nearby castles and left warders at some sites
documented_control_fact: M1516.7 details O'Donnell castle attack assisted by a French knight's artillery ship and takeover at Sligo; garrisons or hostages followed.
Local military authority and foreign arms do not automatically equal English Crown control, or prove exact harbours and shipping routes.

spatial.historical_area_basis: Site-level position only, no entire Sligo/Connacht map under any modern county borders

controls.historical_region: O'Carroll castle in Offaly region, Leim-Ui-Bhanain
controls.legal_claimant: O'Carroll Gaelic lordship and Henry VIII's deputy
controls.effective_authority: Kildare ninth earl military force broke fortifications in 1516
documented_control_fact: M1516.12 records Kildare took fortified O'Carroll castle and destroyed it.
Castle attack not equal to durable crown local governance.

spatial.historical_area_basis: No exact point until historical place-name identity established
